items: Separate Work, Study and Sleep groups containing apps and websites.
New group management; Gouge currently has a single Focus setup.
Choose days, multiple time windows and overnight schedules for profiles.
Extends Gouge's fixed night curfew; can build on A1.
For example, allow YouTube for a total of 30 minutes per day.
Different from the existing limit on each temporary unlock; needs usage access.
Make several apps share one daily allowance instead of separate allowances.
For example, Instagram and YouTube share 30 minutes; needs usage access.
Limit a continuous session, then require a break before using the apps again.
For example, 10 minutes of use followed by a 20-minute break.
Limit how many times an app can be opened in a day.
Counts launches rather than just minutes; needs usage access.
Block everything except selected essentials during a session.
An additional Focus mode; keep emergency and system essentials available.
Alternate focus and break phases for a chosen number of rounds.
Separate from the existing uninterrupted, non-cancellable Focus session.
Lock a profile until a date, for a duration or permanently; allow only tightening.
New profile-level commitment rules; permanent mode would be explicitly opt-in.
Grant a limited extra allowance without removing the underlying daily rule.
Bonus time would use Gouge's delayed approval controls.
Require explicit app approval during a configured window the next day.
Stricter than Gouge automatically releasing a new app when its install wait expires.
Block short-video sections while preserving other parts of supported apps.
Gouge currently has a scrolling watchdog and external Curbox guard; app-version dependent.
Hide supported home feeds, comments or other distracting sections.
For example, keep YouTube search or Instagram messages; app-version dependent.
Apply a daily time limit specifically to Shorts or Reels instead of the whole app.
Requires reliable identification of each supported short-video screen.
Stop access after a chosen number of short videos or swipes.
Distinct from Gouge's rapid-scroll cooldown; counts are heuristic.
Block paths such as youtube.com/shorts while allowing the rest of the site.
Gouge supports temporary path approvals, but its ordered domain rules are host-based.
Add the managed Chrome Google SafeSearch setting.
Applies where Chrome supports the policy; not a filter for every app.
Add managed moderate or strict Restricted Mode for YouTube in Chrome.
Does not force Restricted Mode in the native YouTube app.
Expose managed incognito availability as a protected setting.
Does not replace website or keyword rules.
Manage Chrome Beta, Dev and Canary explicitly as supported browsers.
Gouge currently manages the standard Chrome package directly.
Offer rules for selected translation/archive proxies and data, blob or file URLs.
Optional rules may break legitimate pages; no guarantee against every embedded browser.
Pick a screen element and define a custom hiding or blocking rule.
Advanced feature; selectors and scripts can break after third-party app updates.
Require scanning a paired physical code before an optional unlock.
Needs camera access; does not bypass existing hard Focus locks.
Use a physical NFC tag to start or end a separately configured session.
Needs NFC hardware; applies only to profiles explicitly configured to allow this.
Require typing a chosen sentence before an optional temporary unlock.
Additional friction alongside the chosen delay, not a replacement for it.
Require solving a maths challenge before an optional unlock.
A friction mechanism, not authentication or proof that a person needs access.
Allow only a set number of temporary unlocks during each time period.
Adds a frequency cap to Gouge's existing duration caps.
Turn selected apps grayscale while keeping other apps in colour.
Requires compatible privileged display controls; visual effect needs device testing.
Enable DND during focus sessions or selected schedules and restore it afterwards.
Add a softer session type with explicitly permitted early exits.
Existing non-cancellable Focus remains unchanged unless you explicitly request otherwise.
Prompt a short break after using selected apps for a configured period.
An optional usage-break aid with configurable usage and break durations.
Show daily and weekly usage totals and trends locally.
Needs usage access and explicit local retention settings; website measurement is approximate.
Show how often each app was opened, not only how long it was used.
Display the number of Reels or Shorts scrolled through.
Uses supported-app screen events; counts may be imperfect.
Show estimated time between short-video transitions.
A behaviour estimate; not a scientific measure of attention span.
Display elapsed time over the currently used app.
Requires an overlay-capable service or permission.
Save completed focus sessions, totals and progress towards a chosen goal.
Gouge currently shows the active timer without a full historical dashboard.
Silence chosen apps, including apps that remain otherwise usable.
Needs notification access or DND controls; suspended-app notifications are already hidden by Android.
Hold selected notifications and deliver them at scheduled times.
Needs notification-listener access and careful handling of urgent notifications.
Keep searchable notification history with configurable retention.
Optional storage of private notification content; off unless explicitly selected.
Show network-data totals alongside app usage.
Add home-screen widgets for usage budgets and focus statistics.
Additional to Gouge's existing Focus and Lock apps action widgets.
Support user-selected DNS-over-HTTPS or DNS-over-TLS resolvers.
Gouge currently forwards Google DNS queries over UDP to the network's resolver.
Choose which apps the DNS VPN filters
Expand from Google-only filtering to selected apps or device-wide DNS filtering.
Changes filtering scope and may affect other apps; does not decrypt HTTPS content.
Allow an app to open while denying its network connections.
Needs integration into Gouge's existing VPN rather than starting a competing VPN.
Set network rules for foreground/background use, screen state or metered networks.
A larger networking feature, with possible effects on background messaging.
Offer ad, tracker, malware or content-category lists with update controls.
Separate from Gouge's existing manga-domain watchdog and Google image-host blocklist.
Optionally pin and verify a filtering Private DNS provider through device-owner policy.
System-wide change; needs compatibility testing with the VPN and captive portals.
Route selected app traffic through configured WireGuard or SOCKS tunnels.
Large optional expansion; external endpoints/configuration are required.
Show reader readiness, upstream health, failures and aggregate query timings.
Builds on current VPN status and DNS log; keep sensitive domains out of shared reports.
Paired local parent or accountability app
Manage Gouge from a paired device over the local network.
Separate companion app; signed pairing and command authentication are required.
Manage policies and approvals through a private admin server.
Requires a separately deployed server; Kids Launcher's companion server uses Rust.
Remote lock and timed unlock override
Let an authorised parent or accountability partner send access commands.
Requires F1 or F2; override powers would be explicitly scoped.
Offer a minimal home screen showing only approved apps.
Replaces the phone's home-screen experience; separate from ordinary app suspension.
Restrict Home, Recents, notification shade and other system navigation while pinned.
A substantial change to phone navigation, requiring an explicit exit/recovery design.
Add protected connectivity restrictions and approved quick controls.
Device-owner support varies by Android version and device.
Install, update or remove approved third-party apps through an admin workflow.
Gouge already self-updates; this extends management to other apps.
Offer a deliberately configured emergency override that works without a server.
Would relax selected protections; never silently override existing hard Focus sessions.
Recover a paired management key or account through a recovery phrase.
Recovery primitives and onboarding exist; a complete safe Gouge recovery flow still needs design.
Let an authorised admin request location or ring the managed device.
Requires companion management and explicit location permissions/data handling.
Add an authorised remote wipe command to a managed-device setup.
Destructive and optional; implementation would not execute a wipe during testing.
Upload browser history or journals from explicitly supported companion apps.
Private-data reporting; requires server and matching companion apps, not arbitrary access to all apps.
Serialize reconciliation and reject stale policy snapshots before applying them.
Improve correctness of concurrent VPN, watchdog and unlock changes without blocking the UI.
Record every failed lock/release operation and read back Android's actual state.
Extend Why apps are locked with operation failures and targeted retries.
Let each enforcement step fail and retry without preventing the remaining steps.
Improves existing Gouge recovery rather than adding a second copy of it.
Evaluate reusable packet/DNS parsing, TCP fallback and IPv6 packet support.
A smaller alternative to adopting a complete Go networking engine; benchmark before integration.
Prototype Intra or Firestack integration and retain it only if it improves the required behaviour.
Choose instead of, or benchmark against, I4; not a promise that Go alone makes the VPN faster.
Cache safely with limits, short negative TTLs and current-rule checks.
New blocks and temporary image-access expiry must invalidate or override cached answers.
Use structured, transactional storage and migrations for larger rule/usage datasets.
Useful supporting work for profiles and budgets; not a cosmetic rewrite of the current app.
Bind commands to the device and atomically store replay counters with policy state.
Required foundation for F1/F2/F3; little user-visible value without remote management.
Generate an accurate page of permissions, inspected signals, retained data and sharing.
Registry-driven and tested against actual Gouge behaviour.
Export service health and policy failures without passwords, page text or private URLs by default.
An opt-in Gouge adaptation of the inspected diagnostic patterns.
Test repeated app openings, overlays, wake/reboot, reconnects and allowed-session exits.
Expand the current tests so regressions are caught before installing updates.
Keep repeatable startup, DNS, scan and idle-work measurements with regression thresholds.
Build on existing Gouge profiling; thresholds must come from measurements, not invented scores.
Control selected Curbox groups or focus modes and read approved statistics from Gouge.
Curbox remains a separate app; requires explicit API approval and compatible version/flavour.
Gouge as a Curbox unlock-condition provider
Make Gouge's approved delay or task a required condition for selected Curbox unlocks.
Requires provider registration and a precisely scoped approval; does not expose saved passwords.
Investigate local explicit-image classification as a separate experimental feature.
No ready-made integration for images inside Google or other encrypted apps; capture/privacy/battery design comes first.
Investigate classification beyond Gouge's existing literal keyword rules.
Different from current keyword matching; model access, accuracy and battery use need evaluation.
Activate selected restrictions when entering places such as work or school.
Requires location permission and clear offline/battery behaviour.
Design a time bank earned through approved tasks or activities.
Separate from A10's simple manual bonus allowance; earning verification needs definition.
Provide progressively different presets for younger users, teens or self-control use.
Product presets, not an existing fully verified enforcement engine.
Design a long, visible recovery process for leaving management after loss of the manager.
For example, seven days; would need explicit safeguards and must not silently weaken current commitments.
Investigate an iPhone parent/accountability companion while Gouge remains on Android.
OpenWarden's iOS support is incomplete; this is a separate application project.
Investigate video-CDN activity as an approximate signal.
Not accurate watch-time measurement; cached traffic, shared CDNs and preloading limit it.
